sweep_summary: Polabian (pola1255) is in the catalog as weight-hedged (stress on the last non-reduced syllable: final if its vowel is full, else penult), deciding source Polański 2010, Gramatyka języka połabskiego, sec. 2.2.1 pp. 36-48 (rule p. 48). The search of works with stress or accent in the title turned up a single bibliography item, Eisenberg 1991 'Syllabische Struktur und Wortakzent. Prinzipien der Prosodik deutscher Wörter' (Zeitschrift für Sprachwissenschaft 10(1): 37-64): it is about German word stress, and Glottolog's link to Polabian is a machine keyword assignment (record 411095 language code field: 'Polabian [pox] (computerized assignment from "wortakzent")', page saved). Relevance another language or variety, priority none; the De Gruyter landing page and PDF link could not be reached by automated download/empty to our fetchers (Crossref lists CC BY-NC-ND, so it may open in a browser), not pursued since it says nothing about Polabian; it should be dropped from the pola1255 bibliography. No new Polabian stress source was found; the best first-hand statement read in this search of works with stress in the title is Kortlandt's open 'Polabian accentuation' (already held by the project from the 2026-09-16 check pass), p. 1: 'The stress fell on the last full vowel of a word form, which was found either in the final or in the penultimate syllable. In the latter instance, the final syllable contained a reduced vowel', which confirms the catalog's classification and does not supersede Polański 2010.

new_statements.quote: From a synchronic point of view, the accentuation of Late Polabian has been clarified by Trubetzkoy (1929) and Olesch (1973, 1974). The stress fell on the last full vowel of a word form, which was found either in the final or in the penulti-mate syllable. In the latter instance, the final syllable contained a reduced vowel. This rule was challenged by Kuryłowicz (1955), who maintained that the stress was fixed on the initial syllable of the word. [...] I therefore think that it is correct for an earlier stage of the language, which may conveniently be called Middle Polabian.

new_statements.reading: Late Polabian stress is right-edge and conditioned by vowel quality: it falls on the final syllable when that syllable's vowel is full, otherwise on the penult (the final then having a reduced vowel), i.e. on the last full (non-reduced) vowel of the word form. Kuryłowicz's fixed: initial syllable stress is accepted only for an earlier 'Middle Polabian' stage. This is the same rule as the catalog's deciding source, Polański 2010 p. 48 ('miejscem akcentu połabskiego była ostatnia niezredukowana sylaba wyrazu' = the place of Polabian stress was the last non-reduced syllable of the word; re-verified in the extracted text we hold at, folio 'GP.indb 47'/p. 48), and it confirms the weight-hedged coding (weight = full vs reduced vowel). Note: this file was already downloaded and logged as 'confirms' by the 2026-09-16 check pass ( fetched_now); it was re-read, not newly acquired, in this search of works with stress in the title.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog's weight-sensitive (tentative) coding from Polański 2010 p. 48 ('miejscem akcentu połabskiego była ostatnia niezredukowana sylaba wyrazu' = last non-reduced syllable): final if its vowel is full, else penult; weight class full-vs-reduced vowel; right window. Kortlandt uses the same 'full vowel' vs 'reduced vowel' terms, not long vs short, so he also sides with Polański against reading the rule as vowel-length weight. He adds a diachronic layering (initial stress only for Middle Polabian) that the catalog does not need synchronically. The existing_statements entry for this same file already records this; nothing new.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Late (attested) Polabian: stress falls on the last syllable with a full (non-reduced) vowel; that is the final syllable when its vowel is full, otherwise the penult, in which case the final syllable has a reduced vowel. Right-edge, two-syllable window, 'weight' = full vs reduced vowel. Kuryłowicz's fixed initial stress is accepted by Kortlandt only for an earlier, unattested 'Middle Polabian' stage; pre-Polabian had Proto-Slavic mobile stress. The article's body is a diachronic account of how vowel reduction and the stress shifts produced this surface pattern (retraction from short final vowels, initial fixation, reduction after long vowels, then fixation on the last full vowel).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Late Polabian. Notes that most trisyllabic and all longer word forms have a reduced final vowel (so penult stress generalized there), and that trisyllabic forms with a stressed short medial vowel show no reduction (e.g. *želězo /zil'ozü/); loans are not discussed here (they are in Polański).
new_statements.identity_note: Kortlandt's rule is for 'Late Polabian', i.e. the attested Drawehn (Lüchow-Dannenberg) Polabian of the c. 1700 records; the same variety the catalog codes. His 'Middle Polabian' (initial stress) and 'pre-Polabian' (Proto-Slavic mobile stress) are reconstructed earlier stages, not attested varieties.

tone_statements.citation: Rachwał, Patryk Marek. 2022. Akcent w deklinacji połabskiego rzeczownika w ujęciu diachronicznym [Diachronical view on the word accent in Polabian noun declension]. Zeszyty Łużyckie 57: 71-105.
tone_statements.quote: Tak samo prawdopodobnie było i w języku połabskim: silna redukcja wszystkich zgłosek z wyjątkiem akcentowanych i bezpośrednio przedakcentowych dowodzi, że akcent miał wybitny charakter ekspiratoryczny i znaczną siłę wydechu, czemu towarzyszył zapewne zupełny zanik różnic intonacyjnych między zgłoskami … raczej trzeba przypuszczać, … że nastąpiło to dopiero po zupełnym zatarcia różnic intonacyjnych między poszczególnemi zgłoskami w języku połabskim
tone_statements.translation: The same was probably so in Polabian too: the strong reduction of all syllables except the stressed and immediately pretonic ones proves that the accent had a markedly expiratory character and considerable breath force, which was no doubt accompanied by a complete loss of intonational differences between syllables … rather one must suppose … that this happened only after the complete effacement of intonational differences between the individual syllables in Polabian
tone_statements.summary: Argues attested Polabian had a strong expiratory stress accent and had lost all tonal (intonation) contrasts; for an earlier stage posits a falling (original) vs rising (retracted) accent.

tone_statements.citation: Lehr-Spławiński, Tadeusz (1929). Gramatyka połabska. Lwów: Lwowska Bibljoteka Slawistyczna.
tone_statements.quote: Co do swego cha- rakteru był niewątpliwie silnie ekspiracyjnym, jak wskazują na to redukcje zśłosek nieakcentowanych. Różnice intonacyjne w ostatniej dobie istnienia języka połab- skiego prawdopodobnie nie istniały zupełnie, ale zmiany miejsca akcentu w porównaniu ze stanem prasłow., związane w znacznym stopniu z pierwotnemi różnicami intonacyjnemi dowodzą, że różnice te utrzymywały się dość dłuśo na śruncie połabskim.
tone_statements.translation: As to its character it [the word accent] was undoubtedly strongly expiratory, as the reductions of unaccented syllables show. Intonational differences probably did not exist at all in the last period of the Polabian language's existence, but the changes of the place of accent relative to the Proto-Slavic state, connected to a large degree with the original intonational differences, prove that these differences persisted fairly long on Polabian soil.
tone_statements.locator: p.111, chapter 'Iloczas i akcent', II 'Akcent wyrazowy połabski i jego stosunek do prasłowiańskiego', §103
tone_statements.summary: Word accent was a strong stress (expiratory) accent; pitch distinctions had probably vanished entirely by the language's last stage, though Proto-Slavic intonations conditioned earlier accent shifts.

tone.quote: From these facts we learn that there is really no significant difference between the two accent marks although, if the two marks may coincide in a word, the acute marks the stress and the circumflex a blocked syllable. The fact that the circumflex indicates merely a blocked syllable also tells us that it does not mark any long vowels. … We would expect these newly stressed long vowels to bear the neo-acute accent even though there is no evidence for this in Polabian.

sources.citation: Ambrosiani, Per. 1996. K voprosu o polabskix otraženijax praslavjanskix prosodičeskix otnošenij [On the Polabian reflexes of Proto-Slavic prosodic relations]. In: Rusistika. Slavistika. Indoevropeistika. Sbornik k 60-letiju Andreja Anatol'eviča Zaliznjaka, 346-355. Moskva.
sources.note: Adopts the Lehr-Spławiński/Polański synchronic rule (stress on the last non-reduced vowel, hence final or penult, p. 72) and posits as step 1 of the relative chronology that the Proto-Slavic distinctions between accent types (acute/circumflex/neoacute, i.e. pitch contrasts) were lost, leaving only quantity and stress placement, with quantity itself lost at the last stage (p. 80); Late Polabian thus treated as a dynamic-stress language without tonal contrasts; secondary stress explicitly left aside (p. 72).

tone.quote: [p. 72] Lehr–Spławiński wykazał zaś, że akcent w wyrazach połabskich padał na ostatnią niezredukowaną samogłoskę ... wynika z tego, że akcent padał zawsze na ostatnią lub przedostatnią sylabę wyrazu. Tak też przyjmę w poniższych rozważaniach ... [p. 80] Zakładana chronologia względna przesunięć akcentowych jest następująca: 1. Zanika różnica między różnymi typami akcentu, samogłoski rozróżnia jedynie ogólnolechicki iloczas i obecność lub brak akcentu wyrazowego. ... 5. Ostatecznie zanika iloczas samogłosek. Akcent przesuwa się z pierwszej sylaby na ostatnią sylabę zawierającą samogłoskę niezredukowaną
tone.locator: p. 72 (Wstęp) and p. 80 (section 'Sugerowana chronologia przesunięć akcentowych', items 1 and 5)
tone.translation: [p. 72] Lehr-Spławiński showed that the stress in Polabian words fell on the last non-reduced vowel ... it follows that the stress always fell on the last or the penultimate syllable of the word. This is what I adopt in the discussion below ... [p. 80] The assumed relative chronology of the accent shifts is as follows: 1. The difference between the various types of accent disappears; vowels are distinguished only by Common Lechitic quantity and by the presence or absence of word stress. ... 5. Finally vowel quantity disappears. The stress moves from the first syllable to the last syllable containing a non-reduced vowel
tone.summary: No lexical tone: the Proto-Slavic accent-type (pitch) distinctions are taken to have been lost early in the Lechitic prehistory of Polabian (author's reconstruction, step 1), leaving quantity + stress; Late Polabian has dynamic stress on the last full (non-reduced) vowel = final or penult, quantity finally lost; secondary stress not treated.

sources.note: A study of where the Polabian word accent falls; 'Ton' means accent place. Pitch enters once: inherited Slavic accent quality is said not to affect the shift. No claim about tone in Polabian.

tone.quote: II. In zweisilbigen Paroxytonis geht der Ton im Polabischen anf die letzte Silbe und zwar ohne Einfluss der Accentqualität der ersten Silbe.
tone.translation: II. In disyllabic paroxytona the accent in Polabian goes onto the last syllable, and that without any influence of the accent quality [i.e. inherited Slavic intonation] of the first syllable.
tone.summary: A study of where the Polabian word accent falls; 'Ton' means accent place. Pitch enters once: inherited Slavic accent quality is said not to affect the shift. No claim about tone in Polabian.

tone.quote: Co do swego cha- rakteru był niewątpliwie silnie ekspiracyjnym, jak wskazują na to redukcje zśłosek nieakcentowanych. Różnice intonacyjne w ostatniej dobie istnienia języka połab- skiego prawdopodobnie nie istniały zupełnie, ale zmiany miejsca akcentu w porównaniu ze stanem prasłow., związane w znacznym stopniu z pierwotnemi różnicami intonacyjnemi dowodzą, że różnice te utrzymywały się dość dłuśo na śruncie połabskim.

tone.translation: As to its character it [the word accent] was undoubtedly strongly expiratory, as the reductions of unaccented syllables show. Intonational differences probably did not exist at all in the last period of the Polabian language's existence, but the changes of the place of accent relative to the Proto-Slavic state, connected to a large degree with the original intonational differences, prove that these differences persisted fairly long on Polabian soil.
tone.summary: Word accent was a strong stress (expiratory) accent; pitch distinctions had probably vanished entirely by the language's last stage, though Proto-Slavic intonations conditioned earlier accent shifts.
tone.says: Word accent was a strong stress (expiratory) accent; pitch distinctions had probably vanished entirely by the language's last stage, though Proto-Slavic intonations conditioned earlier accent shifts.
